root_cause.text: An off-by-one bounds error in ocfs2 DLM's dlm_match_regions() used `j <= qr->qr_numregions` when iterating the `qr_regions` array, causing the local-vs-remote region comparison to access one element past the valid end of the remote region list.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `for (j = 0; j <= qr->qr_numregions; ++j)` to `for (j = 0; j < qr->qr_numregions; ++j)` in `fs/ocfs2/dlm/dlmdomain.c`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state this "`<=` instead of `<`" caused a read one entry past the valid range of `qr_regions`.

intent_record.how: This prevents the loop from accessing one element past the end of the remote region array, avoiding an out-of-bounds read while still checking all valid region entries.

candidates.rationale: This loop condition is the direct off-by-one bug: using <= allows j to reach qr->qr_numregions, causing iteration one past the last valid element of the remote region array.
This comparison dereferences the remote-region pointer during the loop; when the preceding off-by-one iteration reaches j == qr->qr_numregions, this statement performs the out-of-bounds access.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop uses <= against qr->qr_numregions, so j reaches qr->qr_numregions and iterates one past the last valid element of the remote qr_regions array, creating the off-by-one out-of-bounds condition described in the root cause.

This statement performs the dereference-based comparison of the remote-region pointer r during the buggy loop iteration. When j == qr->qr_numregions due to the off-by-one loop bound, this memcmp reads past the end of the remote region list.
